items.title: F5 Networks等の複数ベンダの製品における複数の脆弱性
items.body: この問題は、HTTP/2 を使用する NGINX Plus または NGINX オープンソースの構成に影響を及ぼします。NGINX が未公開のトラフィックを処理する際、フロー制御ウィンドウが許容される閾値を超える可能性があり、その結果、通常は NGINX ワーカーがセグメンテーションフォルトを伴うヒープバッファオーバーフローを引き起こすことがあります。さらに、攻撃者はアドレス空間配置のランダム化（ASLR）が無効化されているシステム、または ASLR を回避できる場合にコードを実行することが可能です。影響としては、攻撃者がこの脆弱性を悪用して NGINX ワーカープロセスをクラッシュさせたり、メモリを破損させたり、遠隔でコードを実行したりする恐れがあります。コントロールプレーンへの影響はなく、これはデータプレーンの問題に限られます。注意点としては、技術サポート終了（EoTS）に達したソフトウェアバージョンは評価対象外となります。

items.title: F5 Networks等の複数ベンダの製品における解放済みメモリの使用に関する脆弱性
items.body: NGINX PlusまたはNGINXオープンソースがクライアント接続にHTTP/2を使用するように構成され、クライアントリクエストをバックエンドにプロキシする場合、特別に細工されたリクエストにより、worker_connectionsの残りが少ない状況でワーカープロセスにuse-after-freeが発生する可能性があります。さらに、攻撃者はASLR（アドレス空間配置のランダム化）が無効になっているシステム、またはASLRをバイパスできる場合にコードを実行することが可能です。影響としては、この脆弱性によりリモートの攻撃者がNGINXシステムに対してサービス拒否（DoS）を引き起こすか、コードを実行できる恐れがあります。コントロールプレーンは露出せず、これはデータプレーンの問題に限られます。注として、技術サポート終了（EoTS）に達したソフトウェアバージョンは評価対象外となっています。

items.body: 認証されていないリモートコード実行の脆弱性が、サーベイのパススルー・ルーティングおよびデータインポート処理ロジックに見つかりました。この脆弱性により、悪意のあるユーザーがHTTPリクエストを操作してパブリックサーベイのコンテキストから意図しないコントローラールートへアクセスでき、インポート処理時に細工されたファイルパスやストリームパラメーターを供給して悪用する可能性があります。もし悪用に成功した場合、攻撃者はREDCapサーバー上で任意のコードをリモートで実行できます。攻撃者は認証されている必要はありませんが、悪用するには有効なパブリックサーベイのハッシュを知っている必要があります。この脆弱性はREDCap 13.3.0以降のバージョンに存在します。

items.title: CVE-2026-93585 - An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent ...
items.body:
An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows endpoint with LocalSystem privileges. The affected agent service does not sufficiently enforce authorization restrictions for certain privileged remote management operations. Under specific conditions, the agent fails to apply the intended user impersonation mechanism and executes user-supplied commands within the security context of the agent service, which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

As a result, an authenticated attacker may bypass the intended privilege restrictions and execute arbitrary commands with the highest user-mode privileges on an affected Windows system. Successful exploitation may lead to complete compromise of the affected endpoint, including unauthorized access to sensitive information, modification of system configurations, installation of malicious software, or disruption of system availability. 

The vulnerability does not require administrative credentials or user interaction after successful authentication.

items.body:
Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could carry out more than a simple health check. In deployments that rely on Solr's rule-based authorization, a client granted only the low-privilege health permission could thereby trigger behavior that should require higher privileges; where the shipped security.json template leaves the health permission unauthenticated, no credentials are required at all. 


This issue affects Apache Solr from 9.0.0 through the releases preceding the fixed versions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.11.0 or 10.1.0, which resolve the issue.




You are affected if you run an affected version and allow the /admin/ping endpoint to be reached with only the health permission. This includes the default sample security configuration installed by the bin/solr CLI, where that endpoint is unauthenticated.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict access to the /admin/ping endpoint in their authorization configuration — for example by requiring a trusted role for that path — and ensure Solr is not reachable from untrusted clients or networks, as recommended for all Solr deployments.

items.title: CVE-2026-59442 - TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter does not correctly translate grouped (parenth...

TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter does not correctly translate grouped (parenthesized) filter expressions into the Typesense filter syntax.



As a result, the filter sent to Typesense can have a different meaning than the one the application defined, and some conditions may not be applied as intended.



 An application is affected if it uses the Typesense vector store with filter expressions that contain groups and relies on them to restrict results, for example to enforce tenant isolation or access control.

items.title: CVE-2026-59340 - PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial ...
items.body:
PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial of service when processing untrusted PDF input.



 The underlying text extraction logic reconstructs layout from a PDF's glyph positions and limits how much memory can be allocated for any single computed gap, but does not limit the cumulative allocation across an entire page.



A specially crafted PDF can exploit this to force excessive memory allocation during processing, resulting in OutOfMemoryError.



Depending on JVM configuration, this can cause request failures with degraded service under repeated exploitation, or immediate JVM termination when ExitOnOutOfMemoryError options are used.



Any application that processes PDFs from untrusted sources (document upload, email attachment processing, RAG ingestion, web crawling) using either affected reader is impacted.

items.title: CVE-2026-133867 - @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run insid...
items.body: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.7 through 4.0.9, the plugin does not rewrite regular-expression mount paths to account for a parameterized plugin prefix, so when middleware is mounted with a regular expression inside a plugin registered under a parameterized prefix, the Express matcher treats the prefix parameter as literal text and never matches the real request path. As a result, Express silently skips that middleware while Fastify still runs the route handler, so an application that relies on regular-expression mounted middleware for authentication or authorization inside a parameterized-prefix plugin exposes protected routes to unauthenticated clients. No special configuration is required beyond a parameterized prefix and a regular-expression mount. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-133312 - @fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. S...
items.body: @fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. Starting in version 11.1.0, the plugin documented a manual flow for limiting failed login attempts that peeks at the limiter, runs the password check, and consumes a slot only on failure. Because the peek and the consume are two separate store operations with the password check in between, concurrent requests can all pass the peek before any slot is consumed, so in versions 11.1.0 through 11.2.2 a burst of requests runs far more failed attempts than the configured limit, and the sequential path also allowed one attempt more than configured. The default per-request limiter is not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/rate-limit 11.3.0, which makes the manual flow atomic by reserving a slot in a single operation and refunding it only on success, and users should upgrade to 11.3.0 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-133273 - @fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fasti...
items.body: @fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fastify applications. In versions 2.1.0 through 6.1.4, the authentication hooks that applications register to protect the documentation are applied to every route the plugin adds except the bundled static asset instance. When the option that serves bundled UI files from a local directory is enabled, that instance exposes every file in the directory without credentials, so a specification file an operator meant to keep behind the documentation login becomes reachable by an unauthenticated client who knows or guesses its name. Access is read-only and limited to files in that directory. The issue is fixed in @fastify/swagger-ui 6.1.5, which applies the same authentication hooks to the static asset route, and users should upgrade to 6.1.5 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-133250 - @fastify/middie is the middleware engine for the Fastify web framework. In versi...
items.body: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine for the Fastify web framework. In versions up to and including 9.3.7, middie matches path-scoped middleware against its own reading of the request path, which can differ from the path Fastify's router uses to dispatch the request. When the two disagree, the router can route a request to a handler covered by a middleware mount while middie skips that middleware, so an unauthenticated client reaches a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The mismatch is triggered by empty parameter or wildcard values, request targets that do not begin with a slash, and literal percent characters in a mount path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.8, and users should upgrade to 9.3.8 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-133120 - @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run insid...
items.body: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.10, the plugin passes Express a request URL that does not always match the path Fastify's router dispatched, so path-scoped Express middleware can be skipped while the route handler still runs. Several request forms trigger the mismatch, including percent-decoding that rewrites a backslash to a slash or double-decodes an encoded percent sign, and a request target that begins with an asterisk, so the middleware and the handler disagree on the path or on parameter and query values. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-129850 - @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run insid...
items.body: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-129504 - @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run insid...
items.body: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, the plugin joins a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the Fastify plugin prefix by string concatenation, so when the plugin prefix ends with a slash or the mount path omits its leading slash, the resulting Express mount path does not line up with the route the Fastify router serves. Express then fails to match and passes the request on while the Fastify router still dispatches the route, so the middleware is silently skipped. An application that uses path-scoped Express middleware for authentication or authorization inside a prefixed plugin can expose protected routes to unauthenticated clients, with no crafted request and no non-default option required, and string, array, and regular-expression mount paths are all affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-124626 - @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run insid...
items.body: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.9, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware with a matcher that requires a non-empty value for a dynamic segment, while Fastify's router accepts an empty parameter or wildcard value. When a route and an Express middleware mount share a dynamic pattern, a request with an empty segment matches the Fastify route and runs the handler while the middleware mounted on that pattern is skipped, so on a scoped mount an unauthenticated request can reach a protected handler. No special configuration is required, and the practical impact depends on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

items.body: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
